summary: Defines the WebP image format and registers a media type for it. WebP was developed by Google and was already widely used before this informational RFC documented it.

plainLanguage.summary: WebP is a way of saving pictures in small files so web pages load faster. This document writes down exactly how the format works and gives it an official name tag.

questions: what is the webp image format
subtitle: An efficient image compression format supporting lossy, lossless, animation, and transparency.

tldr.problem: Existing image formats like JPEG, PNG, and GIF each optimize for specific use cases, requiring different formats for different needs. A unified format could reduce file sizes while supporting multiple compression modes.
tldr.mechanism: WebP is a RIFF-based container format that uses VP8 intra-frame encoding for lossy compression and a custom lossless algorithm with LZ77, prefix coding, and color caching. It supports animations, transparency (alpha channels), color profiles (ICC), and metadata (Exif/XMP).
tldr.outcome: WebP reduces file size compared to JPEG, PNG, and GIF for most images, making web pages load faster. Since its development by Google, it has become widely supported in browsers and applications, and this RFC formalizes its specification for the Internet.

facts.label: Lossless compression
facts.value: LZ77 + Huffman prefix codes + color cache

today: WebP is documented in RFC 9649 as an Informational RFC. The format is already widely used on the web and supported by all major browsers, image editing tools, and CDNs.

sections.title: Introduction to WebP
sections.content:
WebP is an image format built on the RIFF (Resource Interchange File Format) container that combines lossy and lossless compression, alpha transparency, animation, and metadata support. It was developed by Google to improve upon JPEG, PNG, and GIF by offering better compression across a wider range of image types.

The format uses two distinct compression algorithms. Lossy compression is achieved using VP8 intra-frame encoding (the same codec behind the VP8 video codec), while lossless compression uses a combination of LZ77 dictionary-based compression, Huffman prefix coding, and a color cache mechanism. This dual approach allows WebP to be significantly smaller than JPEG for photographs and smaller than PNG for images with transparency.
sections.plainLanguage: WebP is like a new way of writing down pictures that saves them in less space than old formats. It can be very good or very detailed, and it works well with many different kinds of images.

sections.title: The WebP Container Structure
sections.content:
A WebP file is organized as a series of chunks following the RIFF file format. Each chunk has a FourCC identifier (four ASCII characters) and a size field, followed by the chunk payload. The file begins with a RIFF header containing the magic string 'WEBP'.

WebP supports three basic file layouts: Simple File Format (Lossy), Simple File Format (Lossless), and Extended File Format. Simple formats are smaller and supported by older software. The extended format includes a VP8X chunk that describes features used in the file, such as whether animation, alpha, Exif metadata, or XMP metadata is present.

The most important chunks are VP8 (for lossy) or VP8L (for lossless) containing the actual image data. Optional chunks include ALPH for alpha transparency, ANIM for animation control, ICCP for color profiles, EXIF and XMP for metadata, and user-defined unknown chunks for extensibility.
sections.plainLanguage: A WebP file is like a box divided into sections, each holding a different piece of information. One section has the picture, and other sections might have color information, animation frames, or a timestamp.

sections.title: Compression Techniques
sections.content:
WebP's lossless compression employs four reversible transforms to reduce entropy: Predictor Transform exploits spatial correlation by encoding only the difference between a pixel and its predicted value; Color Transform reduces correlation between color components; Subtract Green Transform leverages the observation that green channel changes are usually small; and Color Indexing Transform replaces similar colors with indices into a palette.

After transforms, the resulting data is entropy-coded using Huffman prefix codes and an optional color cache that stores recently used colors and can recall them with shorter codes. The format describes the image as subresolution images (entropy images, color transform images, predictor images) that store the statistical encoding information.

For lossy compression, VP8 intra-frame encoding is used, which encodes each frame independently using transform coding (DCT), quantization, and entropy coding, similar to JPEG.
sections.plainLanguage: WebP squeezes pictures down by noticing patterns: pixels next to each other are often similar, colors can be mixed differently, and common colors can be given short names instead of long descriptions.

sections.title: Advanced Features
sections.content:
WebP's extended format supports animation using ANIM and ANMF chunks. The ANIM chunk specifies global parameters like background color and loop count. Each ANMF chunk contains a frame with position, size, duration, and optional blending and disposal methods. This allows canvas-based animation where frames can be partially opaque and previous frames can be cleared or left in place.

The format supports transparency (alpha channel) through the ALPH chunk for lossy images, containing either raw or lossless-compressed 8-bit alpha values. Lossless images (VP8L) can natively include alpha in their pixel data.

Color management is provided via ICC profiles embedded in ICCP chunks. Image metadata can be stored as EXIF (photographic data) or XMP (extensible metadata) in dedicated chunks. All chunks except those critical for reconstruction can be safely ignored by readers that do not support them, providing forward compatibility.
sections.plainLanguage: WebP can do things like show multiple pictures one after another to make an animation, handle transparency so things can look see-through, and remember information about the picture like the date it was taken.

fields.name: RIFF Signature
fields.desc: ASCII 'RIFF' marking the start of a RIFF file.

fields.name: File Size
fields.desc: Size of file minus 8 bytes (for RIFF signature and this field).

fields.name: WEBP Signature
fields.desc: ASCII 'WEBP' identifying this as a WebP file.

fields.name: Flags
fields.desc: Bits indicating presence of animation (A), alpha (L), exif (E), XMP (X), ICC (I).
